description: Pass rules of D31 (photo qualification not_subject and facade QA by registered count): result B of compare (the D31 candidate, fresh runs) against result A (F, the frozen candidate of review-v1), on each split (dev, test) the results record. A copy of review-v1 with the changes stated in decisions; written before the fresh runs. The rules are judged by compare --criteria d31-v1; the checks below them read the run artefacts and are judged outside compare. docs/BENCHMARK.md section 6.2.

A.commons-ten-v1 test: eval/results/commons-ten-v1/f-test.json rescored with a reference cache whose India Gate entry is reference version 2 (benchmark.py rescore --testset commons-ten-v1 --from eval/results/commons-ten-v1/f-test.json): the other four buildings reproduce f-test's metrics, India Gate's reference-based metrics change (docs/BENCHMARK.md section 7.3)

baseline.B: One candidate with both D31 changes (qualification and facade QA), from a commit named before the runs, the same commands as F: synthetic-v1 and mdx-two-v1 --repeat 2; commons-ten-v1 dev (--max-requests brandenburg-gate=104 frauenkirche-dresden=31) and test --repeat 2; --time-cap 3600; stylize on. No ablation run: the qualification is deterministic and every model records its QA path (registration_path).

decisions: D31 (2026-11-03): the owner's rule that a photo's building must be its subject (within 50 m of the OSM outline, or an estimated 1/3 of the frame: Settings.subject_max_distance_m, subject_min_share) and the facade QA count path (6 registered photos with a GPS fit: Settings.qa_face_min_registered). D31 is an owner rule, not a quality claim: the primary cov_local_supported_m_1p5 must not get worse on dev or test, and getting better on dev is not required (review-v1 required it of the adoption program).

In-sample: the share 0.33, the count 6 with its GPS-fit condition and the India Gate reference fix were chosen on F's runs of all ten commons-ten-v1 buildings, the five test buildings included (D31 probes A and B; the 50 m is the owner's figure). The test split is not held out for D31: the fresh runs reproduce the measurement, they do not test it out of sample. The split's rules say a change prompted by test results burns those buildings; the split labels are kept so that dev and test compare with F's results one to one, and cutting a new split version is left to the lead (docs/BENCHMARK.md section 2).

Both A and B score India Gate with reference version 2 (eval_real_landmark.REFERENCE_FIXES: the 13 reference cameras that sit opposite their own GPS and that the photos do not show to be right are marked unverified, 7 of them shown folded onto the west face by more than GPS; docs/BENCHMARK.md section 7.3). inputs_sha256 does not hold the reference version, so compare cannot see a mismatch: check reference_version_2 does.

wrong_face_models_published becomes a hard guard (0 on every building and every repeat) with the corrected reference; review-v1 judged it within noise. With reference version 1 the India Gate east-face models read as wrong-face (probe B on F's runs: the two east-face count-path models at yaw -178 deg against the folded reference): check wrong_face_reference_v1 lists them, they are never counted.

photo_pose_wrong is judged as a rate, photo_pose_wrong / photo_pose_gt_determined, pooled over the split and on every building: worse only when the 95% interval of the difference B - A (Newcombe's hybrid score interval from the two Wilson intervals, benchmark.rate_worse) lies wholly above 0. D31 shows more poses by design (count-path models), so the raw count rises with the poses shown; review-v1's raw-count reading is kept as an info row and as check review_v1_raw_count. The noise is sampling noise because repeats of the same photos do not show it: F's r1 and r2 agree on India Gate (0 of 3 determined poses wrong), where the predicted 4 of 19 would fail on a repeat spread of 0.
Pooled photo_pose_correct must rise (check pose_correct_pooled_rise, over both splits, because dev alone is predicted to move by about the noise); it is an info row per split here.
Cost: within +25% of F per split, cpu_time_s first. jobs_cpu_s is within +25% on both splits (review-v1 asked the persistent map to cut it on dev; D31 makes no cost claim).

Calibration rules are review-v1's. F's test split was INSUFFICIENT on them (4 checked models < 20) and on the struct guards (no structure on three test buildings); the same outcome here is reported with its reason, as for F.
Verdict of D31: FAIL when a rule or a check fails, else INSUFFICIENT when one lacks data, else PASS. compare --criteria d31-v1 judges the rules only and names the checks under its table.

checks.require: India Gate scored with reference version 2 in A and in B; every other building with version 1
checks.how: A: the test result's India Gate record has poses.reference.fix.version 2 (rescore records the reference report). B: the code has eval_real_landmark.REFERENCE_FIXES['india-gate'] version 2, and the India Gate file in the run's --reference-cache has reference_version 2 and the key reference_cache_spec gives now. Other buildings' cache keys are unchanged (tests/test_benchmark.py pins them).
checks.why: inputs_sha256 does not hold the reference version, so compare would compare a version-1 score with a version-2 score without a warning.

checks.require: equal on every repeat of every building
checks.how: Each repeat's summary.json funnel (uploaded, accepted, rejected_by_reason) and, for synthetic-v1, funnel warnings subject_unchecked, against the values below. They come from the offline replay of the D31 qualification step: the product's ingest_upload on every upload of F's runs, in F's order and within F's request caps (F's r1 and r2 upload rows are identical). Every reason other than not_subject equals F's. photos_accepted of every repeat in the result must agree with the funnel.
checks.why: Validation does not depend on SfM, so acceptance is deterministic: any difference is a bug to find, not noise. synthetic-v1 has no bound outline: its acceptance must be F's, with the subject_unchecked warning on every photo with GPS.

checks.require: B - A > noise, pooled over the ten commons-ten-v1 buildings (dev and test results together), with and without India Gate
checks.how: Sum of the recorded photo_pose_correct (median over repeats) of the dev and the test result. Noise: the larger, over A and B, of the sum of the summed buildings' repeat spreads (noise.per_building[slug].photo_pose_correct), as compare bounds a split aggregate. F (India Gate at reference version 2): 167.5 (without India Gate 164.5); F's spreads sum to 3 (Brandenburg 2, Frauenkirche 1). Predicted from probe B's end state: 207.5 (192.5). Per building reported.
checks.why: The point of the count path is more poses shown, as good as F's published facades; India Gate is also judged without, because the split's contamination note reports India Gate apart.

checks.how: Every model of B whose QA passed by the count path (registration_path 'count': details.models[].qa_registration_path, and the summary.json models' qa_checks.registration_path for every repeat), over all commons-ten-v1 buildings and repeats, listed with building, repeat, sector, request, registered/photos, points, published/shown, verified reference cameras, right/wrong and |yaw|. Pooled over these models, right / (right + wrong) over each model's unflagged registered cameras with a verified reference pose (reference version 2), right meaning the model's own camera pose within POSE_RIGHT_M (10 m) and POSE_RIGHT_DEG (15 deg) of the reference, as probe B scored every model: at least 0.745, F's published-facade yardstick (1809 of 2427 poses, 134 models, probe B). Under 100 such poses: INSUFFICIENT. No count-path model with |yaw| >= WRONG_FACE_HEADING_DEG (30 deg) in the geo check against the reference (the wrong_face_models_published test); a model without a yaw (too few verified reference cameras) is listed as unchecked. A full model with registration_path 'count' is a bug.
checks.predicted: Probe B's 75 count-path models on F's runs: 570 of 713 right (0.799) with reference version 2, 570 of 727 (0.784) with version 1; 0 wrong-face with version 2, 4 with version 1 (all India Gate E).
checks.why: The count path is adopted because these models are as good as F's published facades; the yardstick is F's own.

checks.require: with reference version 1, wrong-face models only on India Gate and only in sector E; each listed
checks.how: Optional diagnostic: rescore B from a worktree at 0ebbcc1 (before the reference fix) with the B0 reference cache (India Gate version 1), and list every model counted in wrong_face_models_published (building, repeat, sector, request, registered/photos, yaw).
checks.why: Shows what the folded reference would have reported, so the version-2 zero is not taken on trust.

checks.how: compare --criteria review-v1 with the same A and B: its photo_pose_wrong rows (raw count, pooled and per building) next to this file's rate rule.
checks.why: Expected to flag Lincoln, India Gate and Sagrada: more poses are shown by design.
